title: LOVING YOURSELF
mv: And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
mvp: “And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.” Matthew 22:39
assignment: Identify five (5) areas you have neglected in your life and work on them (2x5=10 Marks).

b.x: Each human being is uniquely created by God. Despite the variations in complexions, sizes, heights, etc., there is something special that stands each person out and makes the individual different from others. You are special (Psalm 139:14). You are a treasure and a neatly wrapped package, which is uncommon in every sphere. You have been designed and configured by God for a reason. You are not a victim of circumstance, irrespective of the incident that may surround your birth or family. Love yourself for who you are, because you are exceptional and in God’s plan.

Each human being is distinctly moulded (Isaiah 64:8) by God, who is the Master Sculptor. The amount of genetic variation-biochemical individuality-between any two humans is approximately 0.1%. Your voice pattern and DNA are like no one else. Your brain is like a supercomputer with about 100 billion neurons, which enables you to think and be motivated by your instincts, intellect and logic. The hairs on your head are numbered (Matthew 10:30) and the colour is divinely created (Matthew 5:36). Humans also possess the creative ability of God Almighty (Exodus 35:30-33). Studies show that the human brain processes about 70,000 thoughts per day.

However, as beautiful as the human creature is, there are still some things that hold individuals down, such as childhood traumas, past mistakes, negative or regrettable actions, low self-confidence, uncomfortable skin colour, size, genetic differences, etc. It is important to attend to all these and move on; confront childhood trauma, forgive yourself and others, build confidence by discovering yourself in the light of God’s word and grow to love yourself with the love God pours in your heart.

As a human being, it is important to love and respect yourself. Avoid comparing yourself to others (2 Corinthians 10:12); instead, strive to be the best version of yourself while learning from others. Recognise your unique identity as a distinct personality (Psalm 139:14) and put your best effort into life’s pursuits (Proverbs 12:24). Work on yourself, seek wisdom (Proverbs 16:16), be a good team player, be proactive and always encourage yourself (1 Samuel 30:6).

Loving yourself involves taking care of your physical and emotional well-being. Dress well, look good and stay cheerful (Proverbs 15:13). Take care of your surroundings (Deuteronomy 23:13-14), eat healthily, exercise (1 Timothy 4:8a), sleep well (Ecclesiastes 5:12) and eliminate negativity such as bitterness (Ephesians 4:31), envy (Proverbs 14:30), and toxic relationships (Proverbs 13:20). Build your self-esteem and stay positively engaged (Ecclesiastes 9:10).

Furthermore, love God passionately (Deuteronomy 6:5) and nurture your relationship with Him daily (2 Peter 3:18). Remember not to elevate any human above God, as true self-love involves recognising God’s supreme position in your life.
Loving yourself is recognition of your uniqueness as God’s creature to fulfil your purpose in life.
